Bounded host link authoring policy v1

This policy governs the first-party native and browser destination-entry controls. It is not a replacement for the portable XML link grammar, authorization, navigation policy or stored-document admission. Existing unsupported destinations and metadata must not be removed or rewritten merely by displaying or editing unrelated text.

New destinations retain their exact input bytes and must satisfy:

  • At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, no raw whitespace, control characters, angle brackets or backslash. Every percent escape has two hex digits; decoded text must be UTF-8 and contain no Unicode control or format characters (categories Cc and Cf).

  • Absolute HTTP/HTTPS with literal ://, nonempty host/authority, no userinfo (including empty userinfo), and any explicit port in 0...65535. Scheme matching is case-insensitive. Encoded spaces and Unicode paths are permitted.

  • Lowercase mailto: with one decoded ASCII recipient. Local part uses letters, digits, dot, underscore, percent, plus or hyphen; no leading/trailing/repeated dot. Domain is dot-separated alphanumeric labels, with internal hyphens allowed. No fragment or authority. Optional query has only unique subject and body key=value pairs, no empty segments, and ASCII URL-safe value characters A-Za-z0-9=%._~+@-. The first equals sign separates key from value; raw ampersands separate parameters. Empty values are permitted; decoded controls are not.

  • Exact lowercase relay:entity/ followed by a lowercase hyphenated UUID. No query, fragment or other suffix. The host still authorizes any navigation; the label remains authored text rather than a server-hydrated title.

link-authoring-policy-v1.json provides shared positive/negative fixtures, including Unicode byte boundaries. Consumers may mirror this small file byte-for-byte when their current package distribution does not ship specification files. This does not expand v1/v2 mark keys or make the host policy a generic RelayMark parser restriction.

Authored AgentSuggestion atom in the optional v3 profile

The draft relaymark-prosemirror-v3 block mapper accepts one root TipTap agentSuggestion atom with a stable relaymarkId and exactly five authored attributes: review, kind, confidence, evidence, and content. Its portable block is relay.agent_suggestion with review, kind, evidence, optional confidence, and one text child holding the Markdown content. The atom has no XML children or second text CRDT.

Only draft and ready are admitted as authored presentation values. accepted and rejected are review decisions, not shared document authority. Proposal IDs, proposal status, undoability, host title, and cached source are absent from the v3 schema and rejected by the strict mapper if supplied. Legacy source-bearing suggestions need deliberate normalization before any v3 enrollment. The ordinary portable directive still supports its broader version 1 contract; this subset does not change it.

content is a nonempty, trimmed Markdown string of at most 32,768 UTF-16 units with no carriage return or NUL. confidence is null or a finite number from 0 to 1. evidence is a unique list of at most 64 nonempty strings, each at most 128 UTF-16 units and free of control characters. Source export uses the existing deterministic directive serializer. The round-trip fixture uses empty evidence. A separate mapper test preserves a same-document block ID in evidence, but such IDs may not resolve after reparsing exported Markdown because the portable source format does not carry them. An ID-preserving export or migration contract is required before live admission of such refs; no implicit remapping is performed.

Concurrent edits to content replace the entire attribute value; they do not merge characters. Live v3 admission remains closed. Host proposal review, accept/dismiss, authorization, and execution stay outside the document.

Draft optional v3 collaborative block identity

This is an unregistered, opt-in contract slice for a future exact relaymark-prosemirror-v3 document schema. It does not add nodes or attributes to the live v1/v2 profiles, admit tables, or change the portable RelayMark AST version. A host may enable it only after browser, server, and native clients negotiate the same new document descriptor and source contract.

Identity on XML and AST blocks

Every Y.XmlElement that the negotiated profile projects to a portable RelayMark AST block carries an explicit relaymarkId XML attribute. Its value is also that block's canonical AST id; it is not a Yjs position, client ID, text hash, or UI key. Y.XmlText and inline marks do not gain a block ID. The current heading headingId remains a separate author-facing Markdown anchor ({#id}), so a heading may carry both attributes. No table, media, or callout AST property mapping is specified by this identity slice.

New collaborative IDs have the form b followed by the 32 lowercase hex digits of a UUIDv4, with hyphens removed. The strict pattern is ^b[0-9a-f]{12}4[0-9a-f]{3}[89ab][0-9a-f]{15}$. It is a subset of the existing portable AST block-ID schema pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$. The prefix is part of the stored ID, so clients do not each invent a different AST projection. IDs are unique within a document and stay with surviving blocks across text edits and moves. A pasted copy gets new IDs; an existing block keeps its ID. A server rejects missing, malformed, or duplicate relaymarkId values for a profile that requires them instead of silently regenerating them during validation.

The browser should use the community TipTap UniqueID extension with attributeName: 'relaymarkId', an explicit list of admitted block node types (including table, tableRow, tableHeader, and tableCell only when tables are separately admitted), and a configured generator that encodes a UUIDv4 in the form above. Filter remote Yjs-origin transactions and mount the editor only after its provider has synced, as the extension documents. Native and server code use their platform UUIDv4 generator and the same encoding; they do not need a second CRDT or a custom node-ID allocator. UniqueID may assign an ID in an appended editor transaction; a future wire fixture must prove that creation plus ID is admitted atomically, or that the host safely groups the updates, before rejecting transient idless states on the live channel. Validate split/merge, paste, undo, and offline concurrent creation before production admission.

Migration boundary

The existing v1→v2 migration remains an exact copy of the Yjs bytes, with no ID rewrite. A later v3 migration first checkpoints and copies the old Yjs bytes into a new incarnation under the existing document/entity locks, then applies and durably records a separate ID-backfill Yjs update while clients are fenced. Only after uniqueness, profile/source projection, and descriptor validation pass may v3 clients join. Preserve the old pending journal and checkpoint under the old incarnation; never replay it blindly into v3. TipTap's automatic initial ID generation must not race across clients as an implicit migration. If an existing portable AST block ID is externally referenced or cannot be preserved under this ID shape, migration must stop for an explicit identity decision rather than silently remap references.

The [ID-only fixture](fixtures/block-identity-v3-draft.json) proves attribute shape and binary Yjs replay. It is not a table AST/source conformance fixture; richer table semantics remain [gated](fixtures/rich-table-ast.pending.json).

Draft optional v3 collaborative block identity

This is an unregistered, opt-in contract slice for a future exact relaymark-prosemirror-v3 document schema. It does not add nodes or attributes to the live v1/v2 profiles, admit tables, or change the portable RelayMark AST version. A host may enable it only after browser, server, and native clients negotiate the same new document descriptor and source contract.

Identity on XML and AST blocks

Every Y.XmlElement that the negotiated profile projects to a portable RelayMark AST block carries an explicit relaymarkId XML attribute. Its value is also that block's canonical AST id; it is not a Yjs position, client ID, text hash, or UI key. Y.XmlText and inline marks do not gain a block ID. The current heading headingId remains a separate author-facing Markdown anchor ({#id}), so a heading may carry both attributes. No table, media, or callout AST property mapping is specified by this identity slice.

New collaborative IDs have the form b followed by the 32 lowercase hex digits of a UUIDv4, with hyphens removed. The strict pattern is ^b[0-9a-f]{12}4[0-9a-f]{3}[89ab][0-9a-f]{15}$. It is a subset of the existing portable AST block-ID schema pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$. The prefix is part of the stored ID, so clients do not each invent a different AST projection. IDs are unique within a document and stay with surviving blocks across text edits and moves. A pasted copy gets new IDs; an existing block keeps its ID. A server rejects missing, malformed, or duplicate relaymarkId values for a profile that requires them instead of silently regenerating them during validation.

The browser should use the community TipTap UniqueID extension with attributeName: 'relaymarkId', an explicit list of admitted block node types (including table, tableRow, tableHeader, and tableCell only when tables are separately admitted), and a configured generator that encodes a UUIDv4 in the form above. Filter remote Yjs-origin transactions and mount the editor only after its provider has synced, as the extension documents. Native and server code use their platform UUIDv4 generator and the same encoding; they do not need a second CRDT or a custom node-ID allocator. The existing v1→v2 migration remains an exact copy of the Yjs bytes, with no ID rewrite. Canonical authored table rendering

The canonical table AST, ProseMirror and XML keep each cell's colspan, rowspan, colwidth and align. Zero or null widths produce an unspecified column; portable rendering adds no minimum width or table sizing policy. Hosts can supply their own presentation defaults without changing the authored document.

fixtures/canonical-table-widths.json is the independent cross-runtime expectation for merged headers, row spans, marked Unicode content and partial widths. Negative/fractional widths and an array whose length differs from the cell's colspan remain invalid under the existing canonical table validator.

The canonical videoEmbed XML/PM node has relaymarkId and videoId only; portable AST is relay.video_embed with props.videoId. Playback provider, processing status, progress, playback/YouTube IDs, title and thumbnail resolve through the host's authorized media domain and view-only presentation storage. args.html:
Native editing runtime

src/content-edit.js is the native editor's runtime, packaged for Swift as RelayMarkSwift/Resources/content-edit-runtime.js and called through RelayMarkContentEditCodec. It runs the maintained ProseMirror schema, model, commands and transform over a document the host has already admitted. It holds no persistence, transport, identity allocation or authority.

  • importDocumentHTML and importClipboardHTML convert HTML through the shared DOM grammar into a canonical document or clipboard slice. The result grants no source, media or edit authority; the host fences the paste and authorizes its references. Clipboard HTML the editor wrote (a ProseMirror slice, or HTML carrying RelayMark identities or authored attributes) must import exactly or is refused. HTML other applications wrote is read with the web editor's own paste rules, the parseHTML rules of the TipTap 3.31 extensions it uses (src/document-html-foreign.js): b, i, s, u, mark, sub, sup, code, inline font-weight, font-style, text-decoration and vertical-align, headings, paragraphs, quotes, lists, task lists, code blocks, tables, rules, breaks, safe links and HTTPS or host media images. Unknown wrappers contribute their content, so Google Docs' font-weight:normal wrapper is not bold.

  • encodeDocumentAttributes and decodeDocumentAttributes convert between logical ProseMirror attributes and physical XML fields (spec/relaymark/xml-attribute-encoding.json).

  • createContentEditCommand(document, {command, selection}) runs one maintained command (return, sink_list_item, lift_list_item or a table command) and returns its actual Steps, the resulting document and selection, and the identities it retained. Linked task items refuse a lift that would discard the linked task.

  • applyContentEdit(document, {kind: "content_edit", steps}) applies actual maintained Step JSON, refusing noncanonical or unknown Steps, and returns the result with the retained, inserted and copied-subtree ranges derived from the actual StepMaps.

  • prepareContentEditWrite(before, steps, after) checks that the Steps produce after and plans the causal ProseMirror-to-Yjs write; planContentEditTextWrite then gives each changed text node its minimal retain/delete/insert delta, so text the edit kept keeps its Yjs items.

  • planClipboardAnchorAllocation and planClipboardHeadingNavigation plan pasted content's Anchor names and heading/link repairs as maintained Steps. Original names never discover pasted nodes by text equality; malformed, unresolved or ambiguous destinations refuse before writing.

Commands and edits keep the 512-Step maximum. A refusal is recoverable; it never falls back to another editor.

args.html:
Draft v3 EntityRef block

This optional offered-node mapping leaves live v3 admission closed. The browser's relayEntityReference is an atom with relaymarkId, entityRef, entityId, entityType, label, projection, and exact authored source. The portable form is {id, type: "relay.entity_reference", props: {id, label, projection, source}, content: []}. The portable ID is the stable relaymarkId; props.id is the authored host entity reference. The atom has no Yjs children, so its authored fallback stays inside props.source rather than acquiring a synthetic child block identity.

The offered subset requires a canonical entity:UUID reference, fixed entityType: "Entity", link/chip/card projection, and one plain fallback line with two-space indentation. It accepts exact LF, CRLF, or CR endings, attribute order, and optional authored label/projection. Source, derived entity UUID, label, and projection must agree with the TipTap attributes. Unknown attributes, hidden children, source drift, and host hydration/action state are rejected. No authorized label, entity fields, action state, or access claim is portable.

The [fixture](fixtures/entity-reference-v3-draft.json) is a real Relay TipTap schema and Yjs update using the community y-tiptap bridge. The generic RelayMark compiler retains exact source for this safe subset and the serializer emits it verbatim. Generic directive compilation retains its existing authored paragraph body; the v3 atom projection has no child content. Both serialize to the same authored source. Native Swift reads the same Yjs update without admitting an editable v3 session. Packaged Elixir validates the same portable AST and exposes RelayMark.parse_v3_entity_reference_source/1 for server admission to compare authored fields with XML attributes. The fallback line is text only; richer directive bodies require a separate mapping with stable child identities.

args.html:
Finite saved form publication import

RelayMark.import_form_publication(publication, namespace: retained_namespace, source: optional_same_release_body) and JS importFormPublication(publication, {namespace, source}) return the canonical document, identity_mapping and explicit normalizations. Elixir wraps success in {:ok, result} and returns content-free diagnostics on refusal. This is a finite migration input decoder; normal editors and respondent renderers consume the canonical document only.

The host retains the complete original publication and its domain fields, including publication identity/time, approval rules, logic and actions. This adapter does not publish, authorize or use a current draft. It converts the historical block list: prose label is complete authored source; question and option labels are rich inline source. The existing canonical importer parses marks, references, callouts, tables, media and other supported prose. Canonical block identities are deterministic from the retained namespace; stable question and option IDs remain exact authored props. Extra question/option settings and answer keys remain portable JSON. Contradictory correctness/answer keys, duplicate identities and ambiguous label/text representations refuse conversion.

When a Course release retained its original body, only that immutable body may be supplied as source. Its prose, question/option identity and rich labels must agree with the saved publication independently of newly allocated block IDs. Missing settings may be recovered from that source with an explicit recover_retained_source_setting normalization. Conflicting known settings or a changed draft label refuse. The publication's grading answer key remains exact. The original publication and exact retained body are both recovery evidence for the host's existing fenced migration receipt.

An absent original body cannot recover information already omitted by a historical parser. Unknown block shapes, unsupported prose or metadata in a fragment refuse loudly. The current canonical questionLabel/option grammar is rich inline: a historical label containing several paragraphs/blocks is an explicit unresolved grammar capability and refuses, rather than flattening it. Normalizations are reviewable evidence, not a claim of publication authorization.

Already canonical publications with a document validate that exact document and return only retained identities with no normalizations. Projected domain blocks are not decoded as historical source; the publication host verifies its own derived block projection against the canonical document. An optional retained source must reconcile to the same semantics without changing canonical identities or recovering new settings on rerun. Invalid current documents fail rather than taking the historical input branch.

This optional mapping preserves ordinary authored PaperButton, PaperAnchor, and PaperConnection as one inert portable block:

The optional relaymark-prosemirror-v3 projector maps the existing TipTap callout and calloutTitle nodes to relay.callout and relay.callout_title blocks. Each block has its own relaymarkId; the title is the first child rather than a string property, so inline marks and a selection anchor can survive a Yjs update. Tone and emphasis use the ordinary editor's enumerated values. The real TipTap/Yjs fixture in fixtures/rich-callout-v3-draft.json covers a bold title between ordinary paragraphs and proves an exact ProseMirror JSON ↔ RelayMark AST inversion.

This parser does not yet express rich title marks or the ordinary editor's full nested Markdown grammar; the versioned AST and exact Yjs bytes remain the portable rich source. Live v3 enrollment stays closed until Phoenix and native project/edit paths, source presentation, migration, and mixed-client recovery pass. Host actions and authorization never belong in the callout node.

Bounded host link authoring policy v1

This policy governs the first-party native and browser destination-entry controls. It is not a replacement for the portable XML link grammar, authorization, navigation policy or stored-document admission. Existing unsupported destinations and metadata must not be removed or rewritten merely by displaying or editing unrelated text.

New destinations retain their exact input bytes and must satisfy:

  • At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, no raw whitespace, control characters, angle brackets or backslash. Every percent escape has two hex digits; decoded text must be UTF-8 and contain no Unicode control or format characters (categories Cc and Cf).

  • Absolute HTTP/HTTPS with literal ://, nonempty host/authority, no userinfo (including empty userinfo), and any explicit port in 0...65535. Scheme matching is case-insensitive. Encoded spaces and Unicode paths are permitted.

  • Lowercase mailto: with one decoded ASCII recipient. Local part uses letters, digits, dot, underscore, percent, plus or hyphen; no leading/trailing/repeated dot. Domain is dot-separated alphanumeric labels, with internal hyphens allowed. No fragment or authority. Optional query has only unique subject and body key=value pairs, no empty segments, and ASCII URL-safe value characters A-Za-z0-9=%._~+@-. The first equals sign separates key from value; raw ampersands separate parameters. Empty values are permitted; decoded controls are not.

  • Exact lowercase relay:entity/ followed by a lowercase hyphenated UUID. No query, fragment or other suffix. The host still authorizes any navigation; the label remains authored text rather than a server-hydrated title.

link-authoring-policy-v1.json provides shared positive/negative fixtures, including Unicode byte boundaries. Consumers may mirror this small file byte-for-byte when their current package distribution does not ship specification files. This does not expand v1/v2 mark keys or make the host policy a generic RelayMark parser restriction.

Authored AgentSuggestion atom in the optional v3 profile

The draft relaymark-prosemirror-v3 block mapper accepts one root TipTap agentSuggestion atom with a stable relaymarkId and exactly five authored attributes: review, kind, confidence, evidence, and content. Its portable block is relay.agent_suggestion with review, kind, evidence, optional confidence, and one text child holding the Markdown content. The atom has no XML children or second text CRDT.

Only draft and ready are admitted as authored presentation values. accepted and rejected are review decisions, not shared document authority. Proposal IDs, proposal status, undoability, host title, and cached source are absent from the v3 schema and rejected by the strict mapper if supplied. Legacy source-bearing suggestions need deliberate normalization before any v3 enrollment. The ordinary portable directive still supports its broader version 1 contract; this subset does not change it.

content is a nonempty, trimmed Markdown string of at most 32,768 UTF-16 units with no carriage return or NUL. confidence is null or a finite number from 0 to 1. evidence is a unique list of at most 64 nonempty strings, each at most 128 UTF-16 units and free of control characters. Source export uses the existing deterministic directive serializer. The round-trip fixture uses empty evidence. A separate mapper test preserves a same-document block ID in evidence, but such IDs may not resolve after reparsing exported Markdown because the portable source format does not carry them. An ID-preserving export or migration contract is required before live admission of such refs; no implicit remapping is performed.

Concurrent edits to content replace the entire attribute value; they do not merge characters. Live v3 admission remains closed. Host proposal review, accept/dismiss, authorization, and execution stay outside the document.

Draft optional v3 collaborative blockentity

This is an unregistered, opt-in contract slice for a future exact relaymark-prosemirror-v3 document schema. It does not add nodes or attributes to the live v1/v2 profiles, admit tables, or change the portable RelayMark AST version. A host may enable it only after browser, server, and native clients negotiate the same new document descriptor and source contract.

Identity on XML and AST blocks

Every Y.XmlElement that the negotiated profile projects to a portable RelayMark AST block carries an explicit relaymarkId XML attribute. Its value is also that block's canonical AST id; it is not a Yjs position, client ID, text hash, or UI key. Y.XmlText and inline marks do not gain a block ID. The current heading headingId remains a separate author-facing Markdown anchor ({#id}), so a heading may carry both attributes. No table, media, or callout AST property mapping is specified by thisentity slice.

New collaborative IDs have the form b followed by the 32 lowercase hex digits of a UUIDv4, with hyphens removed. The strict pattern is ^b[0-9a-f]{12}4[0-9a-f]{3}[89ab][0-9a-f]{15}$. It is a subset of the existing portable AST block-ID schema pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$. The prefix is part of the stored ID, so clients do not each invent a different AST projection. IDs are unique within a document and stay with surviving blocks across text edits and moves. A pasted copy gets new IDs; an existing block keeps its ID. A server rejects missing, malformed, or duplicate relaymarkId values for a profile that requires them instead of silently regenerating them during validation.

The browser should use the community TipTap UniqueID extension with attributeName: 'relaymarkId', an explicit list of admitted block node types (including table, tableRow, tableHeader, and tableCell only when tables are separately admitted), and a configured generator that encodes a UUIDv4 in the form above. Filter remote Yjs-origin transactions and mount the editor only after its provider has synced, as the extension documents. Native and server code use their platform UUIDv4 generator and the same encoding; they do not need a second CRDT or a custom node-ID allocator. UniqueID may assign an ID in an appended editor transaction; a future wire fixture must prove that creation plus ID is admitted atomically, or that the host safely groups the updates, before rejecting transientless states on the live channel. Validate split/merge, paste, undo, and offline concurrent creation before production admission.

Migration boundary

The existing v1→v2 migration remains an exact copy of the Yjs bytes, with no ID rewrite. A later v3 migration first checkpoints and copies the old Yjs bytes into a new incarnation under the existing document/entity locks, then applies and durably records a separate ID-backfill Yjs update while clients are fenced. Only after uniqueness, profile/source projection, and descriptor validation pass may v3 clients join. Preserve the old pending journal and checkpoint under the old incarnation; never replay it blindly into v3. TipTap's automatic initial ID generation must not race across clients as an implicit migration. If an existing portable AST block ID is externally referenced or cannot be preserved under this ID shape, migration must stop for an explicitentity decision rather than silently remap references.

The [ID-only fixture](fixtures/block-identity-v3-draft.json) proves attribute shape and binary Yjs replay. It is not a table AST/source conformance fixture; richer table semantics remain [gated](fixtures/rich-table-ast.pending.json).

Canonical authored table rendering

The canonical table AST, ProseMirror and XML keep each cell's colspan, rowspan, colwidth and align. Static authored HTML preserves those values: cell widths use the maintained comma-separated colwidth attribute, spans stay on the td/th, and the validated alignment appears as both data-align and text-align.

Following the maintained table renderer convention, the first row defines the colgroup. Each spanned column gets its corresponding positive authored pixel width. Zero or null widths produce an unspecified column; portable rendering adds no minimum width or table sizing policy. Hosts can supply their own presentation defaults without changing the authored document.

fixtures/canonical-table-widths.json is the independent cross-runtime expectation for merged headers, row spans, marked Unicode content and partial widths. Negative/fractional widths and an array whose length differs from the cell's colspan remain invalid under the existing canonical table validator.

Canonical authored video

The canonical videoEmbed XML/PM node has relaymarkId and videoId only; portable AST is relay.video_embed with props.videoId. Playback provider, processing status, progress, playback/YouTube IDs, title and thumbnail resolve through the host's authorized media domain and view-only presentation storage. Native RelayMarkNativeSnapshotImport.prepare returns exact originalState and importer result without mutation; the host must preserve both durably before install. Installation checks the same owner, exact original state, vector and snapshot, then applies only the shared importer's recorded attributes on the existing Yrs tree. The original historical video fixture retains the same node/text anchors through migration, then media-adjacent replacement uses actual maintained Steps and converges with a peer. This is local library evidence, not deployed migration.

Nondefault historic media presentation attributes still require corpus/domain classification. The importer currently refuses them with a domain-evidence requirement rather than discarding potential meaning. The first-party web media component documents these fields as server-hydrated presentation values; actual stored exceptions, unresolved IDs and any truly authored metadata must be verified by the host's media owner before broader finite normalization. args.html:
Native editing runtime

src/content-edit.js is the native editor's runtime, packaged for Swift as RelayMarkSwift/Resources/content-edit-runtime.js and called through RelayMarkContentEditCodec. It runs the maintained ProseMirror schema, model, commands and transform over a document the host has already admitted. It holds no persistence, transport,entity allocation or authority.

  • importDocumentHTML and importClipboardHTML convert HTML through the shared DOM grammar into a canonical document or clipboard slice. The result grants no source, media or edit authority; the host fences the paste and authorizes its references. Clipboard HTML the editor wrote (a ProseMirror slice, or HTML carrying RelayMarkentities or authored attributes) must import exactly or is refused. HTML other applications wrote is read with the web editor's own paste rules, the parseHTML rules of the TipTap 3.31 extensions it uses (src/document-html-foreign.js): b, i, s, u, mark, sub, sup, code, inline font-weight, font-style, text-decoration and vertical-align, headings, paragraphs, quotes, lists, task lists, code blocks, tables, rules, breaks, safe links and HTTPS or host media images. Unknown wrappers contribute their content, so Google Docs' font-weight:normal wrapper is not bold.

  • encodeDocumentAttributes and decodeDocumentAttributes convert between logical ProseMirror attributes and physical XML fields (spec/relaymark/xml-attribute-encoding.json).

  • createContentEditCommand(document, {command, selection}) runs one maintained command (return, sink_list_item, lift_list_item or a table command) and returns its actual Steps, the resulting document and selection, and the identities it retained. Linked task items refuse a lift that would discard the linked task.

  • applyContentEdit(document, {kind: "content_edit", steps}) applies actual maintained Step JSON, refusing noncanonical or unknown Steps, and returns the result with the retained, inserted and copied-subtree ranges derived from the actual StepMaps.

  • prepareContentEditWrite(before, steps, after) checks that the Steps produce after and plans the causal ProseMirror-to-Yjs write; planContentEditTextWrite then gives each changed text node its minimal retain/delete/insert delta, so text the edit kept keeps its Yjs items.

  • planClipboardAnchorAllocation and planClipboardHeadingNavigation plan pasted content's Anchor names and heading/link repairs as maintained Steps. Original names never discover pasted nodes by text equality; malformed, unresolved or ambiguous destinations refuse before writing.

Commands and edits keep the 512-Step maximum. A refusal is recoverable; it never falls back to another editor.

args.html:
Draft v3 EntityRef block

This optional offered-node mapping leaves live v3 admission closed. The browser's relayEntityReference is an atom with relaymarkId, entityRef, entityId, entityType, label, projection, and exact authored source. The portable form is {id, type: "relay.entity_reference", props: {id, label, projection, source}, content: []}. The portable ID is the stable relaymarkId; props.id is the authored host entity reference. The atom has no Yjs children, so its authored fallback stays inside props.source rather than acquiring a synthetic child blockentity.

The offered subset requires a canonical entity:UUID reference, fixed entityType: "Entity", link/chip/card projection, and one plain fallback line with two-space indentation. It accepts exact LF, CRLF, or CR endings, attribute order, and optional authored label/projection. Source, derived entity UUID, label, and projection must agree with the TipTap attributes. Unknown attributes, hidden children, source drift, and host hydration/action state are rejected. No authorized label, entity fields, action state, or access claim is portable.

The [fixture](fixtures/entity-reference-v3-draft.json) is a real Relay TipTap schema and Yjs update using the community y-tiptap bridge. The generic RelayMark compiler retains exact source for this safe subset and the serializer emits it verbatim. Generic directive compilation retains its existing authored paragraph body; the v3 atom projection has no child content. Both serialize to the same authored source. Native Swift reads the same Yjs update without admitting an editable v3 session. Packaged Elixir validates the same portable AST and exposes RelayMark.parse_v3_entity_reference_source/1 for server admission to compare authored fields with XML attributes. The fallback line is text only; richer directive bodies require a separate mapping with stable childentities.

args.html:
Finite saved form publication import

RelayMark.import_form_publication(publication, namespace: retained_namespace, source: optional_same_release_body) and JS importFormPublication(publication, {namespace, source}) return the canonical document, identity_mapping and explicit normalizations. Elixir wraps success in {:ok, result} and returns content-free diagnostics on refusal. This is a finite migration input decoder; normal editors and respondent renderers consume the canonical document only.

The host retains the complete original publication and its domain fields, including publicationentity/time, approval rules, logic and actions. This adapter does not publish, authorize or use a current draft. It converts the historical block list: prose label is complete authored source; question and option labels are rich inline source. The existing canonical importer parses marks, references, callouts, tables, media and other supported prose. Canonical blockentities are deterministic from the retained namespace; stable question and option IDs remain exact authored props. Extra question/option settings and answer keys remain portable JSON. Contradictory correctness/answer keys, duplicate identities and ambiguous label/text representations refuse conversion.

When a Course release retained its original body, only that immutable body may be supplied as source. Its prose, question/optionentity and rich labels must agree with the saved publication independently of newly allocated block IDs. Missing settings may be recovered from that source with an explicit recover_retained_source_setting normalization. Conflicting known settings or a changed draft label refuse. The publication's grading answer key remains exact. The original publication and exact retained body are both recovery evidence for the host's existing fenced migration receipt.

An absent original body cannot recover information already omitted by a historical parser. Unknown block shapes, unsupported prose or metadata in a fragment refuse loudly. The current canonical questionLabel/option grammar is rich inline: a historical label containing several paragraphs/blocks is an explicit unresolved grammar capability and refuses, rather than flattening it. Normalizations are reviewable evidence, not a claim of publication authorization.

Already canonical publications with a document validate that exact document and return only retainedentities with no normalizations. Projected domain blocks are not decoded as historical source; the publication host verifies its own derived block projection against the canonical document. An optional retained source must reconcile to the same semantics without changing canonicalentities or recovering new settings on rerun. Invalid current documents fail rather than taking the historical input branch.

args.html:
Draft v3 Paper controls

This optional mapping preserves ordinary authored PaperButton, PaperAnchor, and PaperConnection as one inert portable block:

{id: relaymarkId, type: "relay.paper_control", props: {control, ...authoredFields, source}, content: []}.

control is exactly button, anchor, or connection. A button has label, kind (anchor, link, or command), and target; an anchor has name; a connection has provider. source is the canonical @Button(...), @Anchor(...), or @Connection(...) line generated in the ordinary browser field order with JSON strings. It must exactly agree with the typed fields. The browser nodes do not store a source attribute; the projection derives it. Existing valid ordinary Markdown spellings, including single quotes, spacing, and attribute order, parse into the same typed fields and serialize to this canonical source before v3 enrollment.

The portable contract rejects unknown fields, hidden children, unsafe link or command syntax, source over 16,384 characters, and mismatched source. It carries no navigation result, connection state, host authorization, or hydrated presentation. Hosts decide whether and how to execute or render controls. The [fixture](fixtures/paper-controls-v3-draft.json) contains a real Relay TipTap schema and community Yjs update. This mapping does not admit a live v3 collaboration profile.

args.html:
Draft v3 callout source boundary

The optional relaymark-prosemirror-v3 projector maps the existing TipTap callout and calloutTitle nodes to relay.callout and relay.callout_title blocks. Each block has its own relaymarkId; the title is the first child rather than a string property, so inline marks and a selection anchor can survive a Yjs update. Tone and emphasis use the ordinary editor's enumerated values. The real TipTap/Yjs fixture in fixtures/rich-callout-v3-draft.json covers a bold title between ordinary paragraphs and proves an exact ProseMirror JSON ↔ RelayMark AST inversion.

The @Callout(title: "…", tone: "…", emphasis: "…") { … } source parser can compile a plain title into the same AST shape. This parser does not yet express rich title marks or the ordinary editor's full nested Markdown grammar; the versioned AST and exact Yjs bytes remain the portable rich source. Live v3 enrollment stays closed until Phoenix and native project/edit paths, source presentation, migration, and mixed-client recovery pass. Host actions and authorization never belong in the callout node.

args.html:
Draft v3 image source mapping

This optional mapping extends the unregistered relaymark-prosemirror-v3 authored/default projection. It uses the existing TipTap block image node and the community @tiptap/y-tiptap XML binding. It does not enable live v3 admission or change v1/v2 documents.

An image XML element needs a stable relaymarkId. Its normalized ProseMirror attributes are src, nullable alt, nullable title, and null width and height. The portable AST block is image with the same ID, no children, and props: {src, alt, title}. Only durable /m/ID host media references or HTTPS URLs are accepted. Temporary blob:/data: previews, insecure or credentialed URLs, upload progress, playback/processing state, and dimensions do not enter the portable source. The host still authorizes and resolves media access.

The [fixture](fixtures/rich-image-v3-draft.json) is an actual Yjs update from TipTap 3.30.5 PaperImage, UniqueID, and @tiptap/y-tiptap, with a paragraph on each side. The [test](../../../test/collaboration-rich-image-v3-draft.test.js) checks the Yjs XML, normalized ProseMirror JSON, AST validation, exact inverse, and rejection of temporary media or hidden content. The native YSwift/Yrs read projector and Phoenix/Yex projector replay the same update to that exact AST. This is a source-contract proof only; native image presentation/editing, browser admission, device interaction, and mixed-client live recovery remain gated.

This optional mapping extends the unregistered relaymark-prosemirror-v3 authored/default projection. It uses the existing TipTap block image node and the community @tiptap/y-tiptap XML binding. It does not enable live v3 admission or change v1/v2 documents.

An image XML element needs a stable relaymarkId. Its normalized ProseMirror attributes are src, nullable alt, nullable title, and null width and height. The portable AST block is image with the same ID, no children, and props: {src, alt, title}. Only durable /m/ID host media references or HTTPS URLs are accepted. Temporary blob:/data: previews, insecure or credentialed URLs, upload progress, playback/processing state, and dimensions do not enter the portable source. The host still authorizes and resolves media access.

The [fixture](fixtures/rich-image-v3-draft.json) is an actual Yjs update from TipTap 3.30.5 PaperImage, UniqueID, and @tiptap/y-tiptap, with a paragraph on each side. The [test](../../../test/collaboration-rich-image-v3-draft.test.js) checks the Yjs XML, normalized ProseMirror JSON, AST validation, exact inverse, and rejection of temporary media or hidden content. The native YSwift/Yrs read projector and Phoenix/Yex projector replay the same update to that exact AST. This is a source-contract proof only; native image presentation/editing, browser admission, device interaction, and mixed-client live recovery remain gated.

Draft v3 video source mapping

This optional mapping extends the unregistered relaymark-prosemirror-v3 authored/default projection. It does not change live v1/v2 collaboration or admit v3 editing.

The browser's videoEmbed node contains a durable videoId and hydrated playback, title, source, thumbnail, status, YouTube ID, and upload-progress fields. The portable AST stores only a stable block ID and canonical lowercase UUID: {id, type: "relay.video_embed", props: {videoId}, content: []}. The legacy Markdown directive remains ::video[/v/UUID]. Media authorization and playback metadata remain host-owned. The source projector accepts absent or schema-default values for the hydrated fields, and rejects nondefault values, unknown attributes, hidden children, or malformed IDs.

The [fixture](fixtures/rich-video-v3-draft.json) carries an actual Yjs update produced with TipTap 3.30.5, a videoEmbed node matching the browser's attribute schema, UniqueID using relaymarkId, and @tiptap/y-tiptap 3.0.9. The [test](../../../test/collaboration-rich-video-v3-draft.test.js) checks the XML, exact portable AST and inverse, schema validation, and rejection rules. Swift and server read projectors consume the same update. Native playback and live v3 admission remain separate work.

args.html:
Native editing runtime

src/content-edit.js is the native editor's runtime, packaged for Swift as RelayMarkSwift/Resources/content-edit-runtime.js and called through RelayMarkContentEditCodec. It runs the maintained ProseMirror schema, model, commands and transform over a document the host has already admitted. It holds no persistence, transport,entity allocation or authority.

  • importDocumentHTML and importClipboardHTML convert HTML through the shared DOM grammar into a canonical document or clipboard slice. The result grants no source, media or edit authority; the host fences the paste and authorizes its references. Clipboard HTML the editor wrote (a ProseMirror slice, or HTML carrying RelayMarkentities or authored attributes) must import exactly or is refused. HTML oth er applications wrote is read with the web editor's own paste rules, the parseHTML rules of the TipTap 3.31 extensions it uses (src/document-html-foreign.js): b, i, s, u, mark, sub, sup, code, inline font-weight, font-style, text-decoration and vertical-align, headings, paragraphs, quotes, lists, task lists, code blocks, tables, rules, breaks, safe links and HTTPS or host media images. Unknown wrappers contribute their content, so Google Docs' font-weight:normal wrapper is not bold.

  • encodeDocumentAttributes and decodeDocumentAttributes convert between logical ProseMirror attributes and physical XML fields (spec/relaymark/xml-attribute-encoding.json).

  • createContentEditCommand(document, {command, selection}) runs one maintained command (return, sink_list_item, lift_list_item or a table command) and returns its actual Steps, the resulting document and selection, and the identities it retained. Linked task items refuse a lift that would discard the linked task.

  • applyContentEdit(document, {kind: "content_edit", steps}) applies actual maintained Step JSON, refusing noncanonical or unknown Steps, and returns the result with the retained, inserted and copied-subtree ranges derived from the actual StepMaps.

  • prepareContentEditWrite(before, steps, after) checks that the Steps produce after and plans the causal ProseMirror-to-Yjs write; planContentEditTextWrite then gives each changed text node its minimal retain/delete/insert delta, so text the edit kept keeps its Yjs items.

  • planClipboardAnchorAllocation and planClipboardHeadingNavigation plan pasted content's Anchor names and heading/link repairs as maintained Steps. Original names never discover pasted nodes by text equality; malformed, unresolved or ambiguous destinations refuse before writing.

Commands and edits keep the 512-Step maximum. A refusal is recoverable; it never falls back to another editor.

Bounded host link authoring policy v1

This policy governs the first-party native and browser destination-entry controls. It is not a replacement for the portable XML link grammar, authorization, navigation policy or stored-document admission. Existing unsupported destinations and metadata must not be removed or rewritten merely by displaying or editing unrelated text.

New destinations retain their exact input bytes and must satisfy:

  • At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, no raw whitespace, control characters, angle brackets or backslash. Every percent escape has two hex digits; decoded text must be UTF-8 and contain no Unicode control or format characters (categories Cc and Cf).

  • Absolute HTTP/HTTPS with liter ://, nonempty host/authority, no userinfo (including empty userinfo), and any explicit port in 0...65535. Scheme matching is case-insensitive. Encoded spaces and Unicode paths are permitted.

  • Lowercase mailto: with one decoded ASCII recipient. Loca

    l part uses letters, digits, dot, underscore, percent, plus or hyphen; no leading/trailing/repeated dot. Domain is dot-separated alphanumeric labels, with internal hyphens allowed. No fragment or authority. Optional query has only unique subject and body key=value pairs, no empty segments, and ASCII URL-safe value characters A-Za-z0-9=%._~+@-. The first equals sign separates key from value; raw ampersands separate parameters. Empty values are permitted; decoded controls are not.

  • Exact lowercase relay:entity/ followed by a lowercase hyphenated UUID. No query, fragment or other suffix. The host still authorizes any navigation; the label remains authored text rather than a server-hydrated title.

link-authoring-policy-v1.json provides shared positive/negative fixtures, including Unicode byte boundaries. Consumers may mirror this small file byte-for-byte when their current package distribution does not ship specification files. This does not expand v1/v2 mark keys or make the host policy a generic RelayMark parser restriction.

Bounded host link authoring policy v1

This policy governs the first-party native and browser destination-entry controls. It is not a replacement for the portable XML link grammar, authorization, navigation policy or stored-document admission. Existing unsupported destinations and metadata must not be removed or rewritten merely by displaying or editing unrelated text.

New destinations retain their exact input bytes and must satisfy:

  • At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, no raw whitespace, control characters, angle brackets or backslash. Every percent escape has two hex digits; decoded text must be UTF-8 and contain no Unicode control or format characters (categories Cc and Cf).

  • Absolute HTTP/HTTPS with literal ://, nonempty host/authority, no userinfo (including empty userinfo), and any explicit port in 0...65535. Scheme matching is case-insensitive. Encoded spaces and Unicode paths are permitted.

  • Lowercase mailto: with one decoded ASCII recipient. Local part uses letters, digits, dot, underscore, percent, plus or hyphen; no leading/trailing/repeated dot. Domain is dot-separated alphanumeric labels, with internal hyphens allowed. No fragment or authority. Opti

    onal query has only unique subject and body key=value pairs, no empty segments, and ASCII URL-safe value characters A-Za-z0-9=%._~+@-. The first equals sign separates key from value; raw ampersands separate parameters. Empty values are permitted; decoded controls are not.

  • Exact lowercase relay:entity/ followed by a lowercase hyphenated UUID. No query, fragment or other suffix. The host still authorizes any navigation; the label remains authored text rather than a server-hydrated title.

link-authoring-policy-v1.json provides shared positive/negative fixtures, including Unicode byte boundaries. Consumers may mirror this small file byte-for-byte when their current package distribution does not ship specification files. This does not expand v1/v2 mark keys or make the host policy a generic RelayMark parser restriction.

This is an unregistered, opt-in contract slice for a future exact relaymark-prosemirror-v3 document schema. It does not add nodes or attributes to the live v1/v2 profiles, admit tables, or change the portable RelayMark AST version. Identity on XML and AST blocks

Every Y.XmlElement that the negotiated profile projects to a portable RelayMark AST block carries an explicit relaymarkId XML attribute. Its value is also that block's canonical AST id; it is not a Yjs position, client ID, text hash, or UI key. Y.XmlText and inline marks do not gain a block ID. The current heading headingId remains a separate author-facing Markdown anchor ({#id}), so a heading may carry both attributes. No table, media, or callout AST property mapping is specified by this identity slice.

New collaborative IDs have the form b followed by the 32 lowercase hex digits of a UUIDv4, with hyphens removed. The strict pattern is ^b[0-9a-f]{12}4[0-9a-f]{3}[89ab][0-9a-f]{15}$. It is a subset of the existing portable AST block-ID schema pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$. The prefix is part of the stored ID, so clients do not each invent a different AST projection. IDs are unique within a document and stay with surviving blocks across text edits and moves. A pasted copy gets new IDs; an existing block keeps its ID. A server rejects missing, malformed, or duplicate relaymarkId values for a profile that requires them instead of silently regenerating them during validation.

Filter remote Yjs-origin transactions and mount the editor only after its provider has synced, as the extension documents. Native and server code use their platform UUIDv4 generator and the same encoding; they do not need a second CRDT or a custom node-ID allocator. The existing v1→v2 migration remains an exact copy of the Yjs bytes, with no ID rewrite. Preserve the old pending journal and checkpoint under the old incarnation; never replay it blindly into v3. Bounded host link authoring policy v1

This policy governs the first-party native and browser destination-entry controls. It is not a replacement for the portable XML link grammar, authorization, navigation policy or stored-document admission. Existing unsupported destinations and metadata must not be removed or rewritten merely by displaying or editing unrelated text.

New destinations retain their exact input bytes and must satisfy:

  • At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, no raw whitespace, control characters, angle brackets or backslash. Every percent escape has two hex digits; decoded text must be UTF-8 and contain no Unicode control or format characters (categories Cc and Cf).

  • Absolute HTTP/HTTPS with literal ://, nonempty host/authority, no userinfo (including empty userinfo), and any explicit port in 0...65535. Scheme matching is case-insensitive. Encoded spaces and Unicode paths are permitted.

  • Lowercase mailto: with one decoded

    ASCII recipient. Local part uses letters, digits, dot, underscore, percent, plus or hyphen; no leading/trailing/repeated dot. Domain is dot-separated alphanumeric labels, with internal hyphens allowed. No fragment or authority. Optional query has only unique subject and body key=value pairs, no empty segments, and ASCII URL-safe value characters A-Za-z0-9=%._~+@-. The first equals sign separates key from value; raw ampersands separate parameters. Empty values are permitted; decoded controls are not.

  • Exact lowercase relay:entity/ followed by a lowercase hyphenated UUID. No query, fragment or other suffix. The host still authorizes any navigation; the label remains authored text rather than a server-hydrated title.

Native editing runtime

src/content-edit.js is the native editor's runtime, packaged for Swift as RelayMarkSwift/Resources/content-edit-runtime.js and called through RelayMarkContentEditCodec. It runs the maintained ProseMirror schema, model, commands and transform over a document the host has already admitted. It holds no persistence, transport, identity allocation or authority.

  • importDocumentHTML and importClipboardHTML convert HTML through the shared DOM grammar into a canonical document or clipboard slice. The result grants no source, media or edit authority; the host fences the paste and authorizes its references. Clipboard HTML the editor wrote (a ProseMirror slice, or HTML carrying RelayMark identities or authored attributes) must import exactly or is refused. HTML other applications wrote is read with the web editor's own paste rules, the parseHTML rules of the TipTap 3.31 extensions it uses (src/document-html-foreign.js): b, i, s, u, mark, sub, sup, code, inline font-weight, font-style, text-decoration and vertical-align, headings, paragraphs, quotes, lists, task lists, code blocks, tables, rules, breaks, safe links and HTTPS or host media images. Unknown wrappers contribute their content, so Google Docs' font-weight:normal wrapper is not bold.

  • encodeDocumentAttributes and decodeDocumentAttributes convert between logical ProseMirror attributes and physical XML fields (spec/relaymark/xml-attribute-encoding.json).

  • createContentEditCommand(document, {command, selection}) runs one maintained command (return, sink_list_item, lift_list_item or a table command) and returns its actual Steps, the resulting document and selection, and the identities it retained. Linked task items refuse a lift that would discard the linked task.

  • applyContentEdit(document, {kind: "content_edit", steps}) applies actual maintained Step JSON, refusing noncanonical or unknown Steps, and returns the result with the retained, inserted and copied-subtree ranges derived from the actual StepMaps.

  • prepareContentEditWrite(before, steps, after) checks that the Steps produce after and plans the causal ProseMirror-to-Yjs write; planContentEditTextWrite then gives each changed text node its minimal retain/delete/insert delta, so text the edit kept keeps its Yjs items.

  • planClipboardAnchorAllocation and planClipboardHeadingNavigation plan pasted content's Anchor names and heading/link repairs as maintained Steps. Original names never discover pasted nodes by text equality; malformed, unresolved or ambiguous destinations refuse before writing.

Commands and edits keep the 512-Step maximum. A refusal is recoverable; it never falls back to another editor.

The draft relaymark-prosemirror-v3 block mapper accepts one root TipTap agentSuggestion atom with a stable relaymarkId and exactly five authored attributes: review, kind, confidence, evidence, and content. Its portable block is relay.agent_suggestion with review, kind, evidence, optional confidence, and one text child holding the Markdown content. The atom has no XML children or second text CRDT.

Only draft and ready are admitted as authored presentation values. accepted and rejected are review decisions, not shared document authority. Proposal IDs, proposal status, undoability, host title, and cached source are absent from the v3 schema and rejected by the strict mapper if supplied. Legacy source-bearing suggestions need deliberate normalization before any v3 enrollment. The ordinary portable directive still supports its broader version 1 contract; this subset does not change it.

content is a nonempty, trimmed Markdown string of at most 32,768 UTF-16 units with no carriage return or NUL. confidence is null or a finite number from 0 to 1. evidence is a unique list of at most 64 nonempty strings, each at most 128 UTF-16 units and free of control characters. Source export uses the existing deterministic directive serializer. The round-trip fixture uses empty evidence. A separate mapper test preserves a same-document block ID in evidence, but such IDs may not resolve after reparsing exported Markdown because the portable source format does not carry them. An ID-preserving export or migration contract is required before live admission of such refs; no implicit remapping is performed.

Concurrent edits to content replace the entire attribute value; they do not merge characters. Live v3 admission remains closed. Host proposal review, accept/dismiss, authorization, and execution stay outside the document.

Bounded host link authoring policy v1

This policy governs the first-party native and browser destination-entry controls. It is not a replacement for the portable XML link grammar, authorization, navigation policy or stored-document admission. Existing unsupported destinations and metadata must not be removed or rewritten merely by displaying or editing unrelated text.

New destinations retain their exact input bytes and must satisfy:

  • At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, no raw whitespace, control characters, angle brackets or backslash. Every percent escape has two hex digits; decoded text must be UTF-8 and contain no Unicode control or format characters (categories Cc and Cf).

  • Absolute HTTP/HT

    TPS with literal ://, nonempty host/authority, no userinfo (including empty userinfo), and any explicit port in 0...65535. Scheme matching is case-insensitive. Encoded spaces and Unicode paths are permitted.

  • Lowercase mailto: with one decoded ASCII recipient. Local part uses letters, digits, dot, underscore, percent, plus or hyphen; no leading/trailing/repeated dot. Domain is dot-separated alphanumeric labels, with internal hyphens allowed. No fragment or authority. Optional query has only unique subject and body key=value pairs, no empty segments, and ASCII URL-safe value characters A-Za-z0-9=%._~+@-. The first equals sign separates key from value; raw ampersands separate parameters. Empty values are permitted; decoded controls are not.

  • Exact lowercase relay:entity/ followed by a lowercase hyphenated UUID. No query, fragment or other suffix. The host still authorizes any navigation; the label remains authored text rather than a server-hydrated title.

link-authoring-policy-v1.json provides shared positive/negative fixtures, including Unicode byte boundaries. Consumers may mirror this small file byte-for-byte when their current package distribution does not ship specification files. This does not expand v1/v2 mark keys or make the host policy a generic RelayMark parser restriction.
